presentation.findingName: Privacy-rights disclosure not found in the inspected policy
presentation.suggestedFix:
Open each inspected policy document listed with this finding and locate its consumer-rights section. Confirm the exact missing right against the retained clause assessment. Ask the privacy owner to determine applicability and exceptions; a disclosure finding does not prove requests would be refused.

For each confirmed applicable omission, add plain-language wording explaining that right and how to exercise it. For non-discrimination, explain that exercising privacy rights will not result in prohibited discriminatory treatment; have the privacy owner approve any applicable exception or incentive wording. Do not publish an unreviewed blanket promise or a fictional contact channel.

Publish the approved text as readable HTML under a clear rights heading, with a real request/contact route where required. Keep the policy linked from the scanned page, update its version/date, and clear caches. Check the deployed contact destination with the owner; do not send real personal data or submit a request merely to test discovery.

Re-test: Open the revised policy from the scanned page in a fresh signed-out session. Confirm the specific missing right is now stated in its rights context, and that links resolve to the approved route. Retain the exact passage and URL, obtain privacy-owner sign-off, then re-scan. Legal applicability and fulfillment effectiveness remain separate checks.

presentation.suggestedFix: Perform a targeted DOM audit to resolve the identified WCAG failures. Prioritize Level A remediation: ensure all images have descriptive alt text, interactive elements (buttons/links) have unique aria-labels, and the tabindex sequence is logically structured to prevent keyboard traps in dynamic page components.
presentation.whyThisMatters: The automated detector retained automated accessibility rule examples for review, signaling structural issues in the DOM. In technical auditing, even a low example count can indicate barriers, such as missing ARIA landmarks or broken keyboard focus, that may affect core navigation or interactive elements for users relying on assistive technologies.
